text:
maria: Heads-up — after yesterday's microbatch change (microbatch_size 8 -> 16) EU p99 spiked ~120ms around 03:20 UTC. Initial profiler points at cross-region fallback + kernel swap warm-up. attaching quick trace below.

alex: can you paste the profiler snippet? is this confined to EU only?

maria: yes only EU-primary -> fallback to us-west when local capacity peaks. p95 stayed fine, p99 tail moved.

jordan: curious if it's queueing or kernel overhead. both can blow up p99 w/ fallback fanout.

maria: profiler (trimmed):
```
queue_time_ms=45
kernel_switch_ms=210
kv_miss_rate=0.13
fallback_targets=[us-west]
concurrent_microbatches=4
```

kai: kernel_switch_ms=210 is the red flag. that's warmup/recompile, not normal hot-path. which kernel was selected?

maria: selected kernel= int8_mixed_plan_v3 on origin. fallback worker only has fp16_plan so runtime triggers kernel swap/recompile path.

anya: that mismatch + extra queueing from larger microbatches will amplify tail. KV misses across region add another 50-100ms per request if prefix cache isn't populated.

alex: so theory = microbatch bump increased in-flight concurrency -> local capacity fills -> requests fan out to other region -> those nodes pick different kernel variant -> kernel_swap + kv_miss => p99 spike.

jordan: what about p95 vs p99 tradeoff if we shrink microbatch? p95 probably slightly worse but p99 better. we should quantify.

kai: proposed quick experiment:
- pin kernel variant across regions for the canary (force int8_mixed_plan_v3)
- reduce microbatch cap in EU from 16 -> 6
- bump KV prefix TTL to reduce cross-region miss amplification
run for 2h A/B and compare p95/p99.

maria: +1. also add a guard: if fallback triggers, prefer same-kernel fallback worker or skip kernel-swap path and use slower-compatible kernel to avoid recompile tail.

alex: can we simulate with loadgen to estimate throughput loss? want expected throughput delta at p95 target.

jordan: I'll run synthetic replay with EU traffic profile and the new microbatch settings. should take ~30m to get stable p95/p99.

anya: note: if we pin kernel it may slightly increase token cost due to less optimal kernel on fallback nodes. but cheaper than 200ms p99 hits.

maria: I'll collect flame graphs for both variants and KV hit rate breakdown. sending to #perf-dumps when ready.

sre-bot: flagged incident stub #INC-2026, assigned eng-runtime on-call.

deploy-bot: rolling canary -> eu-inference-pool, overrides: kernel_pin=int8_mixed_plan_v3, microbatch_max=6, kv_prefix_ttl=30m. start in 5m.

maria: monitoring dashboards: eu.p99.latency, kernel_swap.count, kv_miss.rate. will post snapshots at +20m and +60m. :eyes:

alex: if canary looks good, gradually promote to all eu clusters and add policy to prefer kernel-compatible fallback. :thumbsup:

jordan: running the replay now, will post initial numbers in ~35m.

kai: logging note: add a short lived metric `fallback_kernel_mismatch` so we can alert before p99 moves.

maria: thanks team — this matches the earlier suspicion that cross-region routing + kernel mismatch is the main amplifier. follow-ups: replay results, flame graphs, and proposal PR for routing policy and kernel compatibility table.
